cases.given: Plane A durably covers scoped prefix N/hash H; Plane B covers N-1.
cases.when: A caller requests a combined view at N.
cases.then: Refuse with projection lag/unavailable; do not combine A(N) with B(N-1) or silently downgrade the exact request.
cases.invariant: A response binds one verified common ledger prefix.

cases.given: Both cursors report sequence N but different complete scope or head hash.
cases.when: The coordinator considers publishing a common checkpoint.
cases.then: Refuse publication, retain the prior valid checkpoint and investigate the divergence.
cases.invariant: A common sequence number is not a common history identity.

cases.given: A projector computes event effects but crashes before committing its SQLite transaction.
cases.when: It restarts from its durable cursor.
cases.then: No cursor may be ahead of durable rows; reprocess from the last committed prefix without duplicate effects.
cases.invariant: Rows and projector cursor commit atomically within each plane.

cases.given: Both planes committed N, but the coordinator crashed before publishing N.
cases.when: Recovery runs.
cases.then: Verify both committed receipts and the authoritative prefix before publishing once; never manufacture missing rows or replay duplicate effects.
cases.invariant: Publication is recoverable independently of the two store transactions.

cases.given: Manifest N names an absent or corrupt store generation.
cases.when: A query presents that checkpoint handle.
cases.then: Fail that checkpoint closed; rebuild and verify replacement generations before publishing them; do not substitute different bytes under the same handle.
cases.invariant: Checkpoint identity is stable and missing state is not silently accepted.

cases.given: A reader has a live retention pin and open read transactions for old checkpoint M.
cases.when: A projector advances and a compactor attempts to discard M history or delete its store generation.
cases.then: Compaction/deletion cannot remove resources needed by that reader; bounded expiry and transaction completion govern eventual release.
cases.invariant: Published historical reads retain the exact state they reference.

cases.given: A checkpoint retention pin expires before the reader opens its store transactions.
cases.when: The reader tries to proceed using the old handle.
cases.then: Refuse or reacquire and revalidate coverage; never proceed on an unpinned possibly deleted generation.
cases.invariant: A stale retention lease is not permission to read retired state.

cases.given: At seq10 custody B has valid interval [30,infinity). An explicit authorized advance_time commits tick40 by seq12. At seq13, still tick40, custody changes to C.
cases.when: The projector handles seq13 and a reader asks valid40 separately at recorded prefixes12 and13.
cases.then: Retain the superseded B revision and return B at valid40/prefix12; overwriting its sole valid_to=40 and returning no owner is a failure. At valid40/prefix13 return C. Both queries are within their prefix world clock of40.
cases.invariant: Later interval closure does not erase older recorded-prefix answers.

cases.given: Custody changes A-to-B at tick30/seq12 and B-to-C at tick30/seq13.
cases.when: Readers query valid30 separately at prefixes12 and13.
cases.then: Return B then C through recorded revisions; do not collapse both prefixes into C or require a fabricated extra tick.
cases.invariant: Sequence distinguishes equal-tick transitions.

cases.given: A claim occurred at tick10 but A acquisition committed at tick20/seq8.
cases.when: A queries cutoff tick19/seq8 or tick20/seq7.
cases.then: Exclude the claim in both cases; occurrence time cannot satisfy the acquisition cutoff.
cases.invariant: Both acquisition time and recorded sequence constrain knowledge.

cases.given: A acquired a private claim at tick20/seq8; B belongs to the same party but has no disclosure receipt/acquisition.
cases.when: B or a party view queries that prefix.
cases.then: Exclude the claim; party membership cannot union A private knowledge.
cases.invariant: Knowledge requires explicit authorized observers/disclosure.

cases.given: A acquired a claim at20/8; a later authorized disclosure to B commits at24/11.
cases.when: B queries cutoff23/11,24/10, then24/11.
cases.then: The first two exclude it; the last may include it. A original acquisition remains20/8.
cases.invariant: Later transmission creates a later recipient acquisition, not retroactive sharing.

cases.given: A caller supplies a foreign rights lane, actor, party or complete scope with a valid local checkpoint handle.
cases.when: The scoped query service receives the request.
cases.then: Reject authorization before returning records; checkpoint possession does not confer access.
cases.invariant: Authenticated complete scope and viewer authority bind every query.

cases.given: A caller requests an acquisition sequence or tick beyond the checkpoint coverage.
cases.when: The query service evaluates the request.
cases.then: Reject the request; do not fill missing data from a later independently advancing plane.
cases.invariant: An exact query cannot exceed its materialized checkpoint.

cases.given: The published graph checkpoint is20; authority disappearance occurred at25 and naming at27.
cases.when: A present caller requests historical prefix20, or generated text based on20 is ready for delivery.
cases.then: Apply current anomaly restrictions from the authority, suppress prohibited output and do not let the caller select old policy state.
cases.invariant: Historical data cannot roll back current safety policy.

cases.given: A common graph checkpoint is healthy, but current authority anomaly or current entitlement status cannot be obtained.
cases.when: A response or disclosure requiring that policy is ready.
cases.then: Fail closed instead of treating the graph checkpoint or a TTL timestamp as current policy proof.
cases.invariant: Projection freshness and current authorization are separate prerequisites.

cases.given: A player is authorized for an actor knowledge view only.
cases.when: They request the canonical plane, full private event/receipt, seed, raw draw or internal plane/genesis commitment using a selector or checkpoint handle.
cases.then: Reject privileged selectors and do not expose hidden data; only separately allowed v1 blinded RNG outcome fields remain eligible.
cases.invariant: Knowledge references do not confer authority-store access.

cases.given: A visible derived rumor has a source claim that the viewer cannot read.
cases.when: The query includes provenance references or traversal.
cases.then: Do not expose private source content or a fetchable unrestricted reference; apply provenance disclosure rules.
cases.invariant: Provenance cannot bypass the underlying knowledge boundary.

cases.given: A model proposes a backdated correction of custody or a historical assertion under v1.
cases.when: The proposal reaches the projector or authority.
cases.then: Reject the unsupported correction; no insertion into past ledger order or projector-only truth mutation.
cases.invariant: Historical correction requires a separately reviewed authorized event contract.

cases.given: A new-version ID-entry array contains duplicate IDs or is not in the specified lexical order.
cases.when: It is validated as canonical signed/state input.
cases.then: Reject it; do not silently sort or choose the last duplicate before verifying identity.
cases.invariant: A versioned map has one deterministic representation and unique keys.

cases.given: A v2 entry has id constructor or prototype as an allowed scalar string.
cases.when: A bridge attempts to coerce the representation into an unchanged v1 identifier-keyed snapshot/write path.
cases.then: Refuse capability incompatibility before mutation; do not silently rename or promise unchanged v1 support. The reviewed v2 entry-array reader must preserve the scalar exactly.
cases.invariant: Allowed ID values and unsafe object property names are distinct.

cases.given: An otherwise plausible identifier is __proto__ or starts with an underscore.
cases.when: It is presented under the proposed unchanged ASCII/length identifier domain.
cases.then: Reject by the ID grammar before mutation; do not claim __proto__ was a valid v1 ID.
cases.invariant: The first-character rule remains explicit and unchanged.

cases.given: A legacy signed history contains a valid scalar claim ID constructor or case-distinct IDs A and a.
cases.when: Migration attempts to reserve, case-fold or rename those strings.
cases.then: Refuse that lossy migration; preserve original bytes/IDs and verify the legacy history before deriving a new representation.
cases.invariant: Migration never silently changes signed history or existing ID identity.

cases.given: A malformed v1 snapshot has an unsafe object property rejected by the original codec.
cases.when: An importer converts it into a representable v2 entry array.
cases.then: Conversion alone must not authenticate it; reject/quarantine pending separately authorized recovery provenance.
cases.invariant: Representability is not proof of valid legacy history.

cases.given: An ID-bearing DTO has getters, a nonplain prototype or prototype-sensitive object properties.
cases.when: It reaches contract validation or migration.
cases.then: Reject unsafe object structure without executing accessors; allowing matching scalar ID strings does not relax object safety.
cases.invariant: Identifier compatibility does not authorize prototype mutation or accessor execution.

cases.given: A local manifest and both databases are restored together with an older valid journal prefix.
cases.when: A design claims its local checkpoint detects every operator rollback.
cases.then: Reject that assurance claim; require D04 independent anchoring if selected, or document the bounded storage trust model.
cases.invariant: A same-domain projection manifest is not an independent rollback anchor.

cases.given: A v1 world is at tick10 and no clock advance is authorized; its frozen unit is one second.
cases.when: A ten-minute session deadline expires or many wall-clock days pass.
cases.then: World tick, age, lifespan balances and ledger head remain unchanged; the unit definition does not imply wall-clock synchronization.
cases.invariant: Only authorized advance_time changes world time; v1 units/replay remain fixed.

cases.given: A raid and a solo proposal share checkpoint H; the raid commits first.
cases.when: The solo proposal is submitted unchanged against H.
cases.then: Return CONFLICT without implicit queue, rebase, backdated insert or new branch; request fresh context before a changed intent.
cases.invariant: Sessions cannot overwrite another committed expedition past.

cases.given: A party collected multiple proposals against one serialize checkpoint.
cases.when: The first commits and the coordinator tries to replay the rest against the new head without revalidation/confirmation.
cases.then: Reject stale proposals; serialize means ordered authority execution, not silent identity/head rewriting.
cases.invariant: Ordering does not remove per-proposal current-state authorization.

cases.given: A session has awaiting participants or an unconfirmed intent.
cases.when: A timer, disconnection or spotlight rotation occurs.
cases.then: Do not manufacture pass, consent, proposal, observation or clock advancement; update only explicit coordination state.
cases.invariant: Transport pacing is not fictional actor choice.

cases.given: A generated disclosure has not been emitted or acknowledged.
cases.when: The model or coordinator marks it heard or uses it as donor consent.
cases.then: Do not commit acquisition or consent; require the separate authenticated delivery and informed-donor paths.
cases.invariant: Generated prose, knowledge acquisition and consent are different events.

cases.given: A disclosure unit is bound to one scope, content digest and recipient.
cases.when: An acknowledgement changes recipient/scope/bytes or is supplied only by model JSON.
cases.then: Reject the receipt and append no observation.
cases.invariant: Delivery evidence is authenticated and binds exact recipient and content.

cases.given: One disclosure has been acknowledged by A but not B.
cases.when: A shared-party transport retries or an aggregated UI requests both actors knowledge.
cases.then: Create no B acquisition from A receipt; retries reconcile A same delivery key without duplicate observation.
cases.invariant: Party delivery is evaluated per recipient.

cases.given: An observation submission may have appended before cancellation or timeout.
cases.when: The coordinator tries a new proposal ID without reconciling the old one.
cases.then: Refuse that recovery strategy; retry/query the original identity first and use authority-side delivery deduplication before any replacement proposal.
cases.invariant: Cancellation after submission is not proof of no commit.

cases.given: A client acknowledgement at tick30 is not committed as an observation until tick40.
cases.when: A query asks acquisition cutoff30 under the recommended commit-time profile.
cases.then: Exclude it; retain receipt time as separate evidence without backdating acquisition. A different historical-acquisition rule requires review.
cases.invariant: Committed knowledge preserves v1 acquisition semantics.

cases.given: A prepared unit passed an earlier policy check, but a cutoff/revocation is ordered before its actual release gate.
cases.when: The delivery scheduler releases queued content.
cases.then: Suppress the prohibited unit under current policy and create no observation for unsent content; queued authorization is not perpetual permission.
cases.invariant: Current authorization is checked at the defined release point.

cases.given: Only a fragment of a future voice/text unit was transmitted and no complete-unit acknowledgement exists.
cases.when: The coordinator attempts to commit acquisition of the full utterance.
cases.then: Reject full-unit acquisition; partial voice semantics remain unsupported until their versioned protocol is approved.
cases.invariant: Delivery uncertainty cannot invent complete observations.

cases.given: A genuine authorized past delivery has a pending receipt, but membership/rights changed before its observation commit.
cases.when: Recovery attempts blind re-emission or silently discards the evidence.
cases.then: Do neither: retain private evidence, apply the reviewed historical-delivery rules, and fail the unresolved transition closed until those rules exist.
cases.invariant: Past delivery reconciliation is distinct from current permission to disclose again.

cases.given: A caller selects queue or transparent_fork on a first-release checkpoint.
cases.when: The coordinator attempts to run that mode.
cases.then: Return explicit capability unsupported; create neither queue nor branch nor implicit return/merge behavior.
cases.invariant: Reserved mode names do not establish implemented scheduling.

cases.given: An imported genesis has an altered untouched initial balance but the same signed event head.
cases.when: A projector uses only a local genesis hash or store cursor as authentication.
cases.then: Reject that authentication claim; D03 trusted genesis identity/import verification must establish the selected history before trusted rebuild.
cases.invariant: A derived local fingerprint cannot authenticate genesis by itself.

cases.given: A checkpoint world clock is40 and the stored custody interval is open-ended.
cases.when: A caller requests canonical valid time50 or time earlier than supported genesis/retained history.
cases.then: Reject unsupported temporal coverage; do not extrapolate or invent facts from the open interval.
cases.invariant: Recorded intervals do not authorize future prediction or fabricated prehistory.

cases.given: A proposed temporal row has a fractional/unsafe tick or an empty/reversed finite interval.
cases.when: It is validated for projection publication.
cases.then: Reject the invalid row; same-tick historical answers must use recorded revisions rather than invalid intervals.
cases.invariant: All temporal bounds have explicit safe-integer and half-open-interval semantics.

cases.given: A validly signed receipt from a different complete Scope has the same proposal ID, action type, sequence and world time; its signer is valid for both tenants.
cases.when: The bridge verifies it for the original submitted proposal.
cases.then: Reject the complete-scope mismatch before returning an outcome.
cases.invariant: A trusted key and matching short identifiers do not substitute for full namespace binding.

cases.given: Two proposals share ID, kind, expected head/sequence and time, but differ in recipient, amount, causal parents or proxy grant.
cases.when: A receipt for one is returned for the other.
cases.then: Recompute the full canonical proposal digest and reject the mismatch.
cases.invariant: Every submitted proposal field contributes to receipt identity.

cases.given: An authority receipt has a valid signature over its original outcome.
cases.when: An intermediary substitutes event_hash, rng_commitment or another outcome field.
cases.then: Signature verification fails; no modified presentation outcome is accepted.
cases.invariant: The signature covers the complete outcome and all binding fields.

cases.given: An attacker includes a new Ed25519 key and internally valid signatures in a receipt or genesis manifest.
cases.when: The verifier resolves trust for a previously registered scoped ledger.
cases.then: Reject the unregistered signer; do not bootstrap trust from the supplied bundle.
cases.invariant: Cryptographic self-consistency is not authority authentication.

cases.given: The full proposal matches, but the signed submitter is another principal, actor or role.
cases.when: The current caller attempts to accept or retrieve the receipt.
cases.then: Reject subject mismatch and independently enforce current authentication/disclosure policy.
cases.invariant: Historical receipt retrieval is bound to the authenticated subject and does not bypass access control.

cases.given: A donor confirmation is accepted by the existing verifyReceipt(consent, principal) callback.
cases.when: That confirmation is presented as proof that a TELOS outcome came from the expected authority.
cases.then: Reject the substitution; require the separate authority-outcome domain and trusted authority key.
cases.invariant: Donor consent verification and authority outcome verification are different protocols.

cases.given: An action committed, but the transport response was lost.
cases.when: The authenticated caller retries the identical full proposal and ID.
cases.then: Return the original commit identity/receipt after required confirmation; append and apply exactly once and do not reroll.
cases.invariant: Timeout is not proof of non-commit; idempotency binds complete request identity.

cases.given: A caller requires a v2 authenticated receipt, but a legacy peer returns only OutcomeV1.
cases.when: Compatibility negotiation or response validation occurs.
cases.then: Return explicit capability/verification failure; never manufacture scope, proposal identity or a signature.
cases.invariant: No silent downgrade from authenticated receipt assurance.

cases.given: A valid old receipt describes a proxy action committed before the grant was revoked.
cases.when: The holder tries to use that receipt as authorization for another proxy action.
cases.then: The old receipt remains historical evidence only; the new proposal is checked against current revocation state and refused.
cases.invariant: A receipt does not confer future action authority.

cases.given: A trusted manifest commits to the full genesis, and signed events never touch one donor balance.
cases.when: An import changes that balance while retaining the original terminal event head.
cases.then: Reject the recomputed genesis commitment mismatch before authenticated replay.
cases.invariant: Untouched initial state is authenticated independently of which events happen to exercise it.

cases.given: A trusted manifest exists for an empty history whose event head is null.
cases.when: An import changes the private seed or another genesis field.
cases.then: Reject the genesis digest mismatch even though no event signature or RNG record is available.
cases.invariant: Sequence-zero identity cannot depend on a first event or first random draw.

cases.given: A valid private genesis bundle and manifest cover actors, items, parties, world time, scope, ruleset, seed and authority key.
cases.when: Mutate each category separately without changing the trusted manifest.
cases.then: Every mutation fails commitment verification; private nonce replacement also fails.
cases.invariant: The commitment covers the complete genesis bundle, not a selective projection.

cases.given: The current v1 ledger directory contains genesis G and the caller supplies different G2.
cases.when: openLedger opens it, or an open ledger later reads modified genesis.json.
cases.then: Preserve the existing immutable-genesis refusal; do not describe this as a new v2 capability.
cases.invariant: The standalone-import gap does not negate implemented supplied/file genesis checking.

cases.given: An authority holds a full private genesis bundle and an event containing hidden RNG details.
cases.when: It returns an ordinary outcome receipt or public genesis manifest.
cases.then: No seed, private commitment nonce, full random record or authority-only event body is disclosed.
cases.invariant: Commitment/signature verification does not authorize disclosure of their private preimages.

cases.given: A v1 export contains valid event signatures and an expected terminal head but lacks a trusted genesis attestation.
cases.when: It is requested as authenticated standalone history.
cases.then: Refuse that assurance or route only to an explicitly labeled unanchored analysis mode.
cases.invariant: An expected v1 head does not authenticate every genesis field.

cases.given: A legacy bundle may already have lost a valid revocation suffix before a new migration attestation is created.
cases.when: An operator signs the currently supplied bundle without an independently trusted prior checkpoint/source.
cases.then: Do not claim retrospective completeness or rollback resistance; require explicit limited provenance or a trustworthy migration source.
cases.invariant: A new signature cannot prove that missing historical records never existed.

cases.given: Anchored mode witnessed a proxy revocation at sequence N; local events are restored to complete valid prefix N-1.
cases.when: The authority starts or receives another proxy proposal.
cases.then: Fresh witness comparison detects the older prefix and refuses new action processing before proxy validation can authorize it.
cases.invariant: Valid signatures on an older prefix do not defeat a separately retained current checkpoint.

cases.given: The full local directory, snapshot, genesis manifest copy and local checkpoint cache are restored to an old mutually consistent backup; the independent witness remains current.
cases.when: The authority attempts recovery and then a new mutation.
cases.then: Consult the witness and quarantine the stale/conflicting local history; local consistency cannot authorize continuation.
cases.invariant: Whole-directory rollback must not roll back the trust source used to detect it.

cases.given: A proposed anchor shares the journal backup/restore credentials and rollback domain.
cases.when: Both are restored to the same pre-revocation state.
cases.then: The design must not label this independent rollback protection or report detection that the evidence cannot establish.
cases.invariant: A second file, table, Git ref or service name is not an independent trust domain.

cases.given: Anchored mode cannot obtain a fresh authenticated current witness point before starting a mutation.
cases.when: A new proposal arrives, including one using a locally unrevoked grant.
cases.then: Fail unavailable without accepting a new commit or silently switching to trusted_storage mode.
cases.invariant: Strong rollback assurance trades availability for current-state confirmation.

cases.given: A crash occurs before a proposed event is durably appended and the witness still names the predecessor.
cases.when: The authority recovers and the caller retries the same proposal.
cases.then: Perform ordinary current-head validation; no commit or RNG effect is inferred from the interrupted attempt.
cases.invariant: No durable event plus no witness advance does not create an acknowledged mutation.

cases.given: The local journal ends with a partial/torn event and the witness state is separately available.
cases.when: Recovery runs.
cases.then: Fail closed and quarantine; do not silently drop bytes under a generic recovery rule. Any repair requires a reviewed proof that no witnessed event is removed.
cases.invariant: Partial-tail recovery must not become an unchecked history truncation mechanism.

cases.given: One exact complete event was fsynced after the confirmed prefix, but the witness CAS has not completed.
cases.when: Recovery retries after a crash or timeout.
cases.then: Verify and CAS the same signed next event/link; do not reroll, append a replacement or run another action on the pending state.
cases.invariant: There is at most one unconfirmed pending commit per local writer and it retains exact identity.

cases.given: A pending fsynced event exists and the witness remains unavailable.
cases.when: A later player action or current-policy narration request arrives.
cases.then: Remain unavailable for operations requiring confirmed current state; do not expose the pending event as committed or bypass the unresolved append.
cases.invariant: Pending revocation/cutoff recovery cannot be bypassed through ordinary gameplay traffic.

cases.given: The witness accepted an exact event, but its response was lost before the authority recorded success.
cases.when: Recovery or exact caller retry reads the witness.
cases.then: Verify the exact per-sequence head, finalize once and serve the original receipt without a second event.
cases.invariant: An uncertain network response does not duplicate an externally confirmed commit.

cases.given: The event and witness point are durable, but the process crashed before snapshot or receipt delivery.
cases.when: The authority restarts.
cases.then: Replay the confirmed journal, rebuild derived caches and recover the original receipt identity.
cases.invariant: Snapshot and response persistence are not the source of commit authority.

cases.given: The witness is ahead of local durable bytes, whether because of malicious rollback or lost storage.
cases.when: The authority attempts to resume writes.
cases.then: Refuse and recover verified missing event bytes from an authorized source; do not synthesize them from the checkpoint hash.
cases.invariant: Rollback detection does not by itself provide event-data recovery or RPO-zero.

cases.given: Two validly signed candidate heads claim the same registered ledger and sequence, or one substitutes a different genesis digest.
cases.when: A writer calls witness Advance or recovery compares local/witness state.
cases.then: Reject the conflicting CAS/identity and quarantine; do not select by timestamp or signature validity alone.
cases.invariant: The witness retains one ordered registered history, not arbitrary signed heads.

cases.given: An attacker replays an older, correctly signed witness response containing an earlier challenge nonce.
cases.when: A fresh current-read request is awaiting its response.
cases.then: Reject nonce mismatch; a valid old signature cannot satisfy the fresh linearizable-read requirement.
cases.invariant: Authenticity of a checkpoint response is separate from freshness of that response.

cases.given: A rolled-back writer proposes a new history epoch or ledger ID without an authorized migration/registration.
cases.when: It attempts to reset witness state and continue from an older prefix.
cases.then: Refuse reset; retain the registered ledger history and require an explicit predecessor-bound migration.
cases.invariant: Changing identity fields cannot silently bypass rollback protection.

cases.given: The witness current sequence is later than the event named in a receipt.
cases.when: The verifier checks whether the receipt event was actually confirmed.
cases.then: Require the authenticated historical point or specified inclusion evidence matching that event hash; sequence comparison alone is insufficient.
cases.invariant: A larger sequence number is not a proof of ancestry.

cases.given: Deployment explicitly selected trusted_storage mode and both journal and all local checkpoint copies are consistently rolled back.
cases.when: A design or acceptance report evaluates the guarantee.
cases.then: Record that cryptographic rollback detection is outside this mode; do not present prefix validation as detection or relabel this a passing anchored test.
cases.invariant: The supported storage assumption must remain truthful and visible.

cases.given: An anchored-mode authority has fsynced an event but has not confirmed the witness CAS.
cases.when: It is about to publish an outcome receipt, subscriber event or projection checkpoint.
cases.then: Withhold committed success until confirmation; a client deadline yields an uncertain/unavailable result instead.
cases.invariant: Only witness-confirmed events become externally authoritative in anchored mode.

cases.given: A bundle has an authentic complete genesis and a valid historical authority receipt, but no fresh current checkpoint under an assurance policy that requires one.
cases.when: A consumer treats those signatures as proof that the latest revocation/cutoff is present.
cases.then: Reject that freshness inference and enforce the selected current-checkpoint protocol.
cases.invariant: Genesis authenticity, receipt binding and history freshness are separate guarantees.

cases.given: A submitted external-application attempt is VERIFYING with no authenticated verifier receipt.
cases.when: The worker prints success, exits zero, or uploads a forged receipt or a correctly signed receipt copied from another request.
cases.then: No REVIEW, MERGING or MERGED transition occurs; no artifact is accepted and no dependent becomes READY. Only the bound trusted verifier channel and exact current receipt can authorize the next step.
cases.invariant: Worker output and model verdicts cannot attest their own acceptance.

cases.given: The verifier has signed a passing receipt for a fixed repository, board, ticket, epoch, request, run, base, candidate/tree, target ref, policy, runtime and artifact manifest.
cases.when: Each binding is independently changed in a replay, including replay of an otherwise valid receipt from another board or epoch.
cases.then: Signature verification or exact-request comparison rejects every mutation before state advancement or Git mutation.
cases.invariant: An authenticated result is usable only for the exact immutable acceptance request.

cases.given: A profile pins required parent-owned oracles, protected import inventory and normal-completion requirements.
cases.when: A candidate adds an import shadow module, changes pinned tools code, exits before assertions, skips a required case, or prints a counterfeit child completion record.
cases.then: Policy rejects before unsafe import, or the trusted parent records an incomplete/failed check. It emits no passing acceptance receipt merely from the child's claimed results.
cases.invariant: Receipt signing cannot convert an untrusted in-process self-report into independent semantic verification.

cases.given: A verification request is durably reserved and the transport times out without a known execution result.
cases.when: Recovery queries the same request; later an operator closes that run and reserves another, after which the old run reports success.
cases.then: Uncertainty initially retains VERIFYING and path locks. The late old-run receipt is fenced. No process is assumed dead solely from elapsed time, and a stopped run is reaped before replacement is authorized.
cases.invariant: Timeout is not proof of failure or permission to reuse a stale success.

cases.given: An exact request has a durably sealed passing receipt.
cases.when: The same request is retried, followed by a request with the same ID but different bytes.
cases.then: The exact retry returns the original sealed result without another execution. Changed bytes under that ID are refused. Receipt ingestion itself does not merge or duplicate audit transitions.
cases.invariant: Verification retries are idempotent by immutable request identity.

cases.given: Two disjoint application attempts passed verification against the same expected base, and the first has been integrated.
cases.when: The second attempts integration with its original receipt.
cases.then: The changed target base prevents Git mutation. The ticket requires a fresh attempt/candidate and verification, or fails when its configured attempt budget is exhausted. Disjoint paths do not permit an implicit rebase or receipt reuse.
cases.invariant: Acceptance binds the exact tested base and candidate, independently of path disjointness.

cases.given: A repository/ref is registered to board-owned integration, and an integration intent is durably recorded before its ref CAS.
cases.when: The board crashes before CAS while another board or the standalone controller attempts to integrate into the same ref.
cases.then: The shared outstanding-intent reservation blocks the other integrators. Recovery sees the expected base, revalidates evidence and collisions, and executes the original integration once.
cases.invariant: One integration owner and one unresolved intent govern a repository/ref across all boards.

cases.given: Ref CAS reached the exact candidate but checkout or SQLite acceptance has not completed.
cases.when: Recovery is interrupted repeatedly, including during optional re-verification and after its pass but before finalization.
cases.then: The immutable integration intent and path/target locks survive every interruption. Recovery never resets Git to base or releases accepted artifacts early; it completes safe checkout and finalizes the same candidate once.
cases.invariant: Verification-state changes cannot erase an already authorized integration's durable identity.

cases.given: An incoming tracked path collides with an existing ignored file, directory, symlink or non-directory ancestor in the supervisor-owned target checkout.
cases.when: Normal integration runs, or recovery encounters the collision after a previously completed ref CAS.
cases.then: Normal integration refuses before changing the ref. Recovery preserves the local bytes and integrated ref, retains its intent/reservations and withholds artifacts until the collision is explicitly resolved. Safe tracked-only directory replacements remain permitted.
cases.invariant: Git acceptance and recovery never authorize destruction of unrelated local data.

cases.given: An integration intent exists but the target ref now names neither its expected base nor its exact candidate.
cases.when: Recovery runs, including a case where the intended candidate is merely an ancestor of the observed target.
cases.then: The attempt remains unresolved with its target reservation for operator investigation. Recovery does not infer this operation succeeded from ancestry, set MERGED, or expose CAS handoff.
cases.invariant: Observed ancestry is not an authenticated completion record for a specific integration.

cases.given: A passing receipt binds an exact candidate artifact manifest.
cases.when: CAS bytes are corrupted, an object is missing, an old-epoch artifact is substituted, or the manifest changes after verification; repeat before and after ref integration.
cases.then: No downstream artifact is accepted or mounted. Before integration the ref is unchanged; after integration recovery retains the unresolved intent. Any repair reconstructs only the identical committed blob and records that repair, without accepting a different artifact.
cases.invariant: Accepted handoff binds exact candidate bytes, source epoch and receipt, not a mutable ticket label.

cases.given: A passing receipt exists but its verifier key or allowed policy trust generation is revoked before acceptance finalization.
cases.when: The board attempts normal integration or recovery of a ref already advanced to the candidate.
cases.then: The old receipt cannot authorize acceptance. Pre-integration work stops; an integrated candidate remains unresolved without rollback or handoff until a separately authorized fresh proof/recovery decision satisfies current trust policy.
cases.invariant: Trust changes cannot be bypassed by replaying a formerly valid receipt.

cases.given: All required checks and independent review pass for the exact current attempt, candidate, base and manifests.
cases.when: The sole board integrator completes CAS and checkout, commits SQLite finalization, and loses its reply before the caller retries.
cases.then: The retry returns the existing MERGED result without another Git update. Exactly that manifest is accepted, eligible dependents become READY atomically, and the downstream claim pins and rehashes its read-only parent inputs.
cases.invariant: One real integration produces one atomic artifact-acceptance/dependency transition; repeated delivery remains idempotent.

cases.given: A genuine legacy board contains active leases, data-only gate results and interrupted integrations.
cases.when: The reviewed storage migration is interrupted and retried, then a fresh batch adopts the external-application profile.
cases.then: Migration is atomic and preserves legacy identities, locks and audit history. Old passed booleans never become external receipts; retired boards remain truthful. Only newly provisioned immutable profile/key bindings enable new external requests.
cases.invariant: Compatibility migration cannot manufacture acceptance authority or rewrite historical lifecycle outcomes.

cases.given: V1 world_time10, headH, no authorized advance proposal.
cases.when: Advance a fake host clock30 days, poll, reconnect and expire an appointment.
cases.then: World time, actor ages, time balances, RNG counter and ledger head remain unchanged.
cases.invariant: Wall-clock scheduling is not canonical authority.

cases.given: V1 world_time10; a player and a system principal each prepare to_time11.
cases.when: Submit the player proposal, then a current-checkpoint system proposal.
cases.then: Player action appends nothing; system advance sets world_time11 only, without automatic lifespan debit or aging.
cases.invariant: Only explicit authorized advance_time changes the current v1 clock.

cases.given: A solo and a raid proposal share full scope, headH, sequenceS, world_time10 and target the same item.
cases.when: A deterministic barrier lets the raid commit first, then releases solo.
cases.then: Solo returns CONFLICT; exactly one new event exists, with no queue, fork or silent rebase. Reverse the barrier in a separate fixture to reverse the permitted winner.
cases.invariant: Determinism binds accepted ordering; arbitrary network-race winners are not promised.

cases.given: A proposal committed, but its response was lost.
cases.when: Retry the exact proposal bytes and original authenticated principal; separately retry its ID with changed content.
cases.then: Exact retry returns the original outcome and adds no event; changed-content retry conflicts.
cases.invariant: Stable proposal identity reconciles uncertain submission without duplicate effects.

cases.given: One request is cancelled before append; a second loses its response after durable append.
cases.when: Cancel and reconcile each request using its original proposal identity.
cases.then: The pre-append case has zero effects; the post-append case resolves to its one committed result. Do not assert that cancellation undoes committed effects.
cases.invariant: Transport cancellation is not a rollback acknowledgement.

cases.given: ActorA privately acquired claimR at tick10/sequence5; A and B are members of the same genesis party.
cases.when: Query B and the party view without an explicit party disclosure.
cases.then: R is absent; no union of members private claim sets is returned.
cases.invariant: Party membership alone never shares private acquisition.

cases.given: A permitted source occurrence at tick5 is newly observed at tick12/sequence8 by actorA and explicitly disclosed to the fixture party.
cases.when: Query at time11/sequence8, time12/sequence7, and time12/sequence8.
cases.then: Only the final authorized query includes the new record; acquired_at is12, never5.
cases.invariant: Occurrence time cannot backdate acquisition, and both prefix/time cutoffs apply.

cases.given: Proposed deliveryD binds full scope, recipientA and payload digestP; narration was generated but no recipient acknowledgement exists.
cases.when: Simulate send failure, then an acknowledgement for a different payload or recipient.
cases.then: No acquisition commit is accepted. A matching acknowledgement may request one separately authorized observation at its eventual commit time.
cases.invariant: Generated prose, attempted delivery and mismatched acknowledgements do not create knowledge.

cases.given: A matching acknowledgement for deliveryD was accepted and its observation committed; a duplicate acknowledgement arrives after reconnect.
cases.when: Process the duplicate with the stable observation proposal/claim identity.
cases.then: Return the original committed identity with one claim/event total; do not create a later duplicate acquisition.
cases.invariant: Delivery retries are idempotent across the transport-to-observation boundary.

cases.given: A queued narrative payload was prepared before an anomaly cutoff, but release occurs after the cutoff commits.
cases.when: Reauthorize at the recipient release boundary; also request a historical view.
cases.then: Forbidden exposition is suppressed for release and historical presentation. If a prior release is uncertain, record uncertainty instead of claiming the information was erased.
cases.invariant: Current presentation policy cannot be bypassed by stale payloads or historical time.

cases.given: Proposed authority-only assessment: bridge passable at20, destroyed at30; old report acquired byA at40.
cases.when: Assess the report at20 and40 and request A views before and after40.
cases.then: Authority may mark the report outdated at40 without equating it to originally false; acquisition remains40 and assessment metadata is absent from narrator text/ranking.
cases.invariant: Canonical truth, temporal assessment, provenance and actor acquisition are different records.

cases.given: V1 fixture requests queue or transparent_fork checkpoint policy, or a checkpoint with expires_at equal to world_time.
cases.when: Pass the checkpoint to proposal coordination/subscriber validation.
cases.then: Unsupported modes and expiry are refused before planner execution; no canonical events or RNG draws occur.
cases.invariant: Reserved modes and expired checkpoints cannot imply supported scheduling.

cases.given: Proposed hd-tick-fixture/1 declares2 entities,1 project per entity,2 ticks per invocation,2 candidates per tick and4 effects per tick.
cases.when: Exercise each bound atM-1,M,M+1 and integer overflow using synthetic configuration/action records.
cases.then: Within-bound cases have explicit oracles; oversized/overflow cases reject without partial state, RNG or cursor updates, not by silently omitting entities.
cases.invariant: Finite work budgets are validated inputs, not measured production capacity.

cases.given: Proposed pure finite planner at world100, authorized target104, fixed policy/genesis/input proposals and stable slot identities.
cases.when: Process2+2 ticks versus1+1+1+1; permute input entity-map insertion order.
cases.then: Final state, cursor104 and per-slot commitments match after canonical entity ordering; whole event hashes are compared only when envelope identities/order/key are also identical.
cases.invariant: Invocation batching and map iteration do not alter deterministic rule effects.

cases.given: A proposed tick contains one valid resource effect and one unauthorized gift/consent or out-of-jurisdiction Fate effect.
cases.when: Validate the complete tick under the authority writer boundary.
cases.then: Reject all effects; world clock, durable cursor, resources, head and RNG remain at the prior checkpoint.
cases.invariant: Planner output cannot partially commit or manufacture authority/consent.

cases.given: Pure fixture entityA has resource1 and project progress3/4 at100; one follow-up can be created.
cases.when: Process tick101.
cases.then: Exactly one resource is spent and one project completes; resource0 remains; the follow-up cannot execute before102 and cannot invent replenishment.
cases.invariant: Completion cascades are bounded; initial stock equals remaining plus recorded spend.

cases.given: A proposed logical tick committed but the projector/scheduler response or cache write was interrupted.
cases.when: Restart from durable accepted events and reconcile the original tick/proposal identity.
cases.then: Apply committed effects once; rebuild cursor from those effects; never expose a cursor beyond the common committed prefix.
cases.invariant: Durable cursor and effect acceptance recover together without duplicate ticks.

cases.given: V1 fixture has private seed and rng_counterK; an invalid proposal and narrator invocation precede an accepted draw.
cases.when: Reject the invalid proposal, generate mock prose, then submit one valid system draw and replay.
cases.then: Rejection/prose do not incrementK; the accepted draw increments once and replay verifies value/nonce/commitment. Public outcomes omit seed and hidden value.
cases.invariant: Current v1 RNG semantics remain unchanged and authority-private.

cases.given: Proposed migrated slot identity binds scope, ruleset/policy, tick, entity, project, slot and distribution/bound parameters with a private test seed.
cases.when: Change HTTP retry IDs, batching and arrival timing while retaining identical accepted inputs; then change a true slot input.
cases.then: Incidental changes preserve slot commitments; the changed true input belongs to a different slot. This is a proposed migration oracle, not a v1 claim.
cases.invariant: Retry IDs must not become random-outcome fishing inputs.

cases.given: A stochastic planner emitted different proposalsP andQ for the same initial view; accepted execution recorded exactP bytes and input/policy digests.
cases.when: Replay the accepted trace with the planner unavailable or returningQ.
cases.then: Replay consumes recordedP and yields the same accepted state; it does not invoke the model or assertP equalsQ. Q needs a separate current authorization decision.
cases.invariant: Deterministic replay concerns captured accepted inputs, not reproducible LLM generation.

cases.given: Proposed target104 is explicitly authorized from100, with a per-invocation budget of2 ticks.
cases.when: Run one invocation, then pause host time for30 days and reconnect without renewed processing.
cases.then: At most102 is processed; remaining backlog is explicit. Host elapsed time adds no further target, effects or lifespan debit.
cases.invariant: Authorization bounds the target and work budgets bound each invocation.
